title: ack_always: Sender/Receiver embed 1280-byte buffer instead of borrowing
description:
Both Sender and Receiver in ack_always.rs statically allocate MAX_PACKET_SIZE (1280 bytes) arrays:
- Sender: line 54 `packet: [u8; MAX_PACKET_SIZE]`
- Receiver: line 302 `buffer: [u8; MAX_PACKET_SIZE]`

This means every instance is 1.3KB+ regardless of actual packet size. On embedded targets with limited RAM, this is wasteful.

What goes wrong: Memory pressure on constrained devices. Every sender/receiver pair consumes 2.5KB+ of RAM even for small packets.

Compare to AckOnErrorSender which takes `payload: &'a [u8]` - a reference that lets the caller control storage.

Files: /Volumes/Attic/Desktop/Projects/crates/schc/src/fragment/ack_always.rs
close_reason: Refactored ack_always Sender to use borrowed payload reference instead of embedded 1280-byte buffer
